revision.text: 難波神社とは大阪府大阪市中央区博労町4丁目1番3号にある神社。創建は伝・反正天皇。天慶6年（943年）に天王寺区上本町に遷座、慶長2年(1597年)現在地に遷座、昭和20年(1945年)空襲により全焼、昭和 49年(1974年)に再建され現在に至る。主祭神は仁徳天皇、配祀は素盞嗚尊。秋祭（例祭）は10月20日。

{{神社| 名称=難波神社| 所在地=大阪府大阪市中央区博労町4丁目1番3号| 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|}}| 祭神=[[仁徳天皇]]、[[素盞嗚尊]]| 社格=| 創建=伝 反正天皇| 例祭=秋祭(10/20)| 本殿=| 神事=| 画像=[[Image:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|250px]]}} '''難波神社'''（なんばじんじゃ）とは[[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[中央区 (大阪市)|中央区]][[船場 (大阪市)|博労町]]4丁目1番3号にある神社。主祭神は[[仁徳天皇]]、配祀は[[素盞嗚尊]]。秋祭（例祭）は[[10月20日]]。
== 由緒 == 創建は[[反正天皇]]と伝えられ、当初は大阪府[[松原市]]に鎮座していた。[[天慶]]6年（[[943年]]）に現在の[[天王寺区]][[上本町]]に遷座、[[慶長]]2年''([[1597年]]'')現在地に遷座、[[昭和]]20年（[[1945年]]）空襲により全焼、昭和49年（[[1974年]]）に再建され現在に至る。

[[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に[[豊臣秀吉]]の命令で、立退料2,000石をもらって現在地に遷座。しかし、慶長20年（[[1615年]]）の[[大坂の陣|大坂夏の陣]]後には[[江戸幕府]]によって境内地の9割を没収される。
[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）3月13日・14日の第1回[[大阪大空襲]]で焼失するが、[[1974年]]（昭和49年）7月に再建される。
== 祭神 == *主祭神 - [[仁徳天皇]] *配祀 - [[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]
== 境内 == *本殿 *拝殿 *博労[[稲荷神社]] - 祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂尊]]。摂社。商売繁盛の神様として[[船場]]の多くの商人から篤い信仰を受けていた。[[江戸時代]]を通じて難波神社は[[仁徳天皇]]を祀った神社としてではなく、博労稲荷神社がある神社として有名であり、難波神社のこと自体を指して「稲荷社」と呼んでいた。 *[[金刀比羅神社]] - 祭神：[[大物主]]神 *十四柱相殿神社 - 祭神：左殿（[[豊臣秀吉]]公・[[菅原道真]]公・[[楠正成]]公・[[徳川家康]]公）、中殿（[[トヨウケビメ|豊受姫大神]]・[[天照皇大神]]・[[応神天皇]]）、右殿（[[ミヅハノメ|水波能女大神]]・[[春日神|春日四柱大神]]・[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦大神]]・[[カグツチ|迦具土大神]]） *御神木の[[クスノキ|楠]] - 大阪市の保存木第1号。樹齢約400年。
== 祭礼 == *2月節分 節分祭・玉の緒祭 *6月8日 菖蒲神事 *7月20・21日 夏祭・氷室祭 *10月20日 例祭・秋祭 *11月 火焚祭 *毎月1日・2月節分 湯立神楽

{{神社 |名称=難波神社 |所在地=[[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[中央区 (大阪市)|中央区]][[船場 (大阪市)|博労町]]4丁目1-3 {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=12|type=point}} |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}} |祭神=[[仁徳天皇]]、[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]] |社格=旧[[府社]] |創建=伝・[[反正天皇]]の時代 |例祭=秋祭（10月20日） |本殿= |別名=難波上社 |神事= |画像=[[File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|250px]]}} '''難波神社'''（なんばじんじゃ）は、[[大阪市]][[中央区 (大阪市)|中央区]][[船場 (大阪市)|博労町]]にある[[神社]]。[[近代社格制度|社格]]は府社。[[摂津国]][[総社]]として難波大宮または平野神社、他にも上難波[[仁徳天皇]]宮、上難波神社、難波上宮ともいう。[[江戸時代]]には博労稲荷神社がある為に[[稲荷社]]と呼ばれていた。
== 歴史 == 創建は[[反正天皇]]の時代と伝えられ、当初は現在の[[大阪府]][[松原市]]に鎮座していたという。[[天慶]]6年（[[943年]]）に現・[[天王寺区]][[上本町]]に遷座する。
[[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に[[豊臣秀吉]]の命令で、立退料2,000石をもらって現在地に遷座。しかし、慶長20年（[[1615年]]）の[[大坂の陣|大坂夏の陣]]後には[[江戸幕府]]によって境内地の9割を没収される。
[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）3月13日・14日の第1回[[大阪大空襲]]で焼失するが、[[1974年]]（昭和49年）7月に再建される。
== 祭神 == * 主祭神 - [[仁徳天皇]] * 配祀 - [[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]
== 境内 == * 本殿 - [[1974年]]（[[昭和]]49年）7月再建。 * 拝殿 - 1974年（昭和49年）7月再建。 * 博労[[稲荷神社]] - 祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂尊]]。摂社。商売繁盛の神様として[[船場]]の多くの商人から篤い信仰を受けていた。[[江戸時代]]を通じて難波神社は仁徳天皇を祀った神社としてではなく、博労稲荷神社がある神社として有名であり、難波神社のこと自体を指して「稲荷社」と呼んでいた。 * [[金刀比羅神社]] - 祭神：[[大物主]]神 * 十四柱相殿神社 - 祭神：左殿（[[豊臣秀吉]]公・[[菅原道真]]公・[[楠正成]]公・[[徳川家康]]公）、中殿（[[トヨウケビメ|豊受姫大神]]・[[天照皇大神]]・[[応神天皇]]）、右殿（[[ミヅハノメ|水波能女大神]]・[[春日神|春日四柱大神]]・[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦大神]]・[[カグツチ|迦具土大神]]） * 社務所 * 御神木の[[クスノキ|楠]] - 大阪市の保存木第1号。樹齢約400年。
== 祭礼 == * 2月節分 節分祭・玉の緒祭 * 6月8日 菖蒲神事 * 7月20・21日 夏祭・氷室祭 * 10月20日 例祭・秋祭 * 11月 火焚祭 * 毎月1日・2月節分 湯立神楽
== 関連項目 == * [[難波八阪神社]] - 別名は難波下社。 * [[生國魂神社]] - 別名は難波大社。 * [[高津宮]] - 難波神社と同様に[[仁徳天皇]]を主祭神とする。
== 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Namba-jinja}} * [http://www.nanba-jinja.or.jp/ 難波神社]（公式HP） {{神道 横}}

== 概要 == [[摂津国]][[総社]]として難波大宮または平野神社、他にも上難波[[仁徳天皇]]宮、上難波神社、難波上宮ともいう。[[江戸時代]]には博労稲荷神社がある為に[[稲荷社]]と呼ばれていた。
[[アヤメ|アヤメ類]]（厳密な分類の[[ハナショウブ|花菖蒲]]）に縁のある神社で、6月にはあやめ祭（菖蒲神事）で花菖蒲を奉納する神事が執り行われている。境内で育った花菖蒲を御神前に御供えする神事。祭典中、菖蒲を刈り取る所作のある神楽「菖蒲刈り」が二人の巫女によって舞われます。
神紋は[[アヤメ#文様|菖蒲紋]]の一種『抱き菖蒲』（だきあやめ）。
== 歴史 == 創建は[[反正天皇]]の時代と伝えられ、当初は現在の[[大阪府]][[松原市]]に鎮座していたという。[[天慶]]6年（[[943年]]）に現・[[天王寺区]][[上本町]]に遷座する。
[[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に[[豊臣秀吉]]の命令で、立退料2,000石をもらって現在地に遷座。しかし、慶長20年（[[1615年]]）の[[大坂の陣|大坂夏の陣]]後には[[江戸幕府]]によって境内地の9割を没収される。
[[明治]]時代になると[[府社]]に列せられている。[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）3月13日・14日の第1回[[大阪大空襲]]で焼失するが、[[1974年]]（昭和49年）7月に再建される。
== 祭神 == * 主祭神：[[仁徳天皇]] * 配祀：[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]
== 境内 == * 本殿：[[1974年]]（[[昭和]]49年）7月再建。 * 拝殿：1974年（昭和49年）7月再建。 * 博労[[稲荷神社]]：祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂尊]]。摂社。商売繁盛の神様として[[船場]]の多くの商人から篤い信仰を受けていた。[[江戸時代]]を通じて難波神社は仁徳天皇を祀った神社としてではなく、博労稲荷神社がある神社として有名であり、難波神社のこと自体を指して「稲荷社」と呼んでいた。 * [[金刀比羅神社]]：祭神：[[大物主]]神 * 十四柱相殿神社：祭神：左殿（[[豊臣秀吉]]公・[[菅原道真]]公・[[楠正成]]公・[[徳川家康]]公）、中殿（[[トヨウケビメ|豊受姫大神]]・[[天照皇大神]]・[[応神天皇]]）、右殿（[[ミヅハノメ|水波能女大神]]・[[春日神|春日四柱大神]]・[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦大神]]・[[カグツチ|迦具土大神]]） * 社務所 * 御神木の[[クスノキ|楠]]：大阪市の保存木第1号。樹齢約400年。
== 祭礼 == * 2月節分 節分祭・玉の緒祭 * 6月8日 菖蒲神事 * 7月20・21日 夏祭・氷室祭 * 10月20日 例祭・秋祭 * 11月 火焚祭 * 毎月1日・2月節分 湯立神楽
== 関連項目 == * [[難波八阪神社]]：別名は難波下社。 * [[生國魂神社]]：別名は難波大社。 * [[高津宮]]：難波神社と同様に[[仁徳天皇]]を主祭神とする。

[[アヤメ|アヤメ類]]（厳密な分類の[[ハナショウブ|花菖蒲]]）に縁のある神社で、6月にはあやめ祭（菖蒲神事）で花菖蒲を奉納する神事が執り行われている。境内で育った花菖蒲を御神前に御供えする神事。祭典中、菖蒲を刈り取る所作のある神楽「菖蒲刈り」が二人の巫女によって舞われます。
神紋は[[アヤメ#文様|菖蒲紋]]の一種『抱き菖蒲』（だきあやめ）。
== 歴史 == 創建は[[反正天皇]]の時代と伝えられ、当初は現在の[[大阪府]][[松原市]]に鎮座していたという。[[天慶]]6年（[[943年]]）に現・[[天王寺区]][[上本町]]に遷座する。
[[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に[[豊臣秀吉]]の命令で、立退料2,000石をもらって現在地に遷座。しかし、慶長20年（[[1615年]]）の[[大坂の陣|大坂夏の陣]]後には[[江戸幕府]]によって境内地の9割を没収される。
[[明治]]時代になると[[府社]]に列せられている。[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）3月13日・14日の第1回[[大阪大空襲]]で焼失するが、[[1974年]]（昭和49年）7月に再建される。
== 祭神 == * 主祭神：[[仁徳天皇]] * 配祀：[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]]
== 境内 == * 本殿：[[1974年]]（[[昭和]]49年）7月再建。 * 拝殿：1974年（昭和49年）7月再建。 * 博労[[稲荷神社]]：祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂尊]]。摂社。商売繁盛の神様として[[船場]]の多くの商人から篤い信仰を受けていた。[[江戸時代]]を通じて難波神社は仁徳天皇を祀った神社としてではなく、博労稲荷神社がある神社として有名であり、難波神社のこと自体を指して「稲荷社」と呼んでいた。 * [[金刀比羅神社]]：祭神：[[大物主]]神 * 十四柱相殿神社：祭神：左殿（[[豊臣秀吉]]公・[[菅原道真]]公・[[楠木正成]]公・[[徳川家康]]公）、中殿（[[トヨウケビメ|豊受姫大神]]・[[天照皇大神]]・[[応神天皇]]）、右殿（[[ミヅハノメ|水波能女大神]]・[[春日神|春日四柱大神]]・[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦大神]]・[[カグツチ|迦具土大神]]） * 社務所 * 御神木の[[クスノキ|楠]]：大阪市の保存木第1号。樹齢約400年。
== 祭礼 == * 2月節分 節分祭・玉の緒祭 * 6月8日 菖蒲神事 * 7月20・21日 夏祭・氷室祭 * 10月20日 例祭・秋祭 * 11月 火焚祭 * 毎月1日・2月節分 湯立神楽
== 関連項目 == * [[難波八阪神社]]：別名は難波下社。 * [[生國魂神社]]：別名は難波大社。 * [[高津宮]]：難波神社と同様に[[仁徳天皇]]を主祭神とする。
== 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Namba-jinja}} * [http://www.nanba-jinja.or.jp/ 難波神社]（公式HP） {{神道 横}} {{shinto-stub}}

{{混同|難波八阪神社}} {{神社 |名称 = 難波神社 |画像 = [[画像:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|270px]]
拝殿 {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=12|type=point}} |所在地 = [[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[中央区 (大阪市)|中央区]][[博労町 (大阪市)|博労町]]4丁目1-3 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}} |祭神 = [[仁徳天皇]]、[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]] |社格 = 旧[[府社]] |創建 = 伝・[[反正天皇]]の時代 |例祭 = 秋祭（10月20日） |本殿 = |別名 = 難波上社 |神事 = }} '''難波神社'''（なんばじんじゃ）は、[[大阪市]][[中央区 (大阪市)|中央区]][[博労町 (大阪市)|博労町]]にある[[神社]]。旧[[近代社格制度|社格]]は[[府社]]。 == 概要 == [[摂津国]][[総社]]として難波大宮または平野神社、他にも上難波[[仁徳天皇]]宮、上難波神社、難波上宮ともいう。[[江戸時代]]には博労稲荷神社がある為に[[稲荷社]]と呼ばれていた。 [[アヤメ]]類（厳密な分類の[[ハナショウブ|花菖蒲]]）に縁のある神社で、6月にはあやめ祭（菖蒲神事）で花菖蒲を奉納する神事が執り行われている。境内で育った花菖蒲を御神前に御供えする神事。祭典中、菖蒲を刈り取る所作のある神楽「菖蒲刈り」が2人の巫女によって舞われる。 神紋は[[アヤメ#文様|菖蒲紋]]の一種『抱き菖蒲』（だきあやめ）。 == 歴史 == 創建は[[反正天皇]]の時代と伝えられ、当初は現在の[[大阪府]][[松原市]]に鎮座していたという。[[天慶]]6年（[[943年]]）に現・[[天王寺区]][[上本町]]に遷座する。 [[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に[[豊臣秀吉]]の命令で、立退料2,000石をもらって現在地に遷座。しかし、慶長20年（[[1615年]]）の[[大坂の陣|大坂夏の陣]]後には[[江戸幕府]]によって境内地の9割を没収される。 [[明治]]時代になると[[府社]]に列せられている。[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）3月13日・14日の第1回[[大阪大空襲]]で焼失するが、[[1974年]]（昭和49年）7月に再建される。 == 祭神 == * 主祭神：[[仁徳天皇]] * 配祀：[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]] == 境内 == * 本殿 - [[1974年]]（[[昭和]]49年）7月再建。 * 拝殿 - 1974年（昭和49年）7月再建。 * 博労[[稲荷神社]] - 祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂尊]]。摂社。商売繁盛の神様として[[船場]]の多くの商人から篤い信仰を受けていた。[[江戸時代]]を通じて難波神社は仁徳天皇を祀った神社としてではなく、博労稲荷神社がある神社として有名であり、難波神社のこと自体を指して「稲荷社」と呼んでいた。 * [[金刀比羅神社]] - 祭神：[[大物主]]神 * 十四柱相殿神社 - 祭神：左殿（[[豊臣秀吉]]公・[[菅原道真]]公・[[楠木正成]]公・[[徳川家康]]公）、中殿（[[トヨウケビメ|豊受姫大神]]・[[天照皇大神]]・[[応神天皇]]）、右殿（[[ミヅハノメ|水波能女大神]]・[[春日神|春日四柱大神]]・[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦大神]]・[[カグツチ|迦具土大神]]） * 社務所 == 祭礼 == * 2月節分 - 節分祭・玉の緒祭 * 6月8日 - 菖蒲神事 * 7月20・21日 - 夏祭・氷室祭 * 10月20日 - 例祭・秋祭 * 11月 - 火焚祭 * 毎月1日・2月節分 - 湯立神楽 == 文化財 == === 大阪市指定保存樹 === * 御神木の[[クスノキ|楠]] - 大阪市の保存樹第1号である。樹齢約400年。 == 関連項目 == * [[難波八阪神社]] - 別名：難波下社。 * [[生國魂神社]] - 別名：難波大社。 * [[高津宮]] - 難波神社と同様に[[仁徳天皇]]を主祭神とする。 == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Namba-jinja}} * [https://www.nanba-jinja.or.jp/ 難波神社]（公式HP） {{shinto-stub}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:なんはしんしや}} [[Category:大阪市の神社]] [[Category:総社 (地域)]] [[Category:稲荷神社]] [[Category:大阪府の旧府社]] [[Category:大阪市中央区の建築物]] [[Category:大阪市中央区の歴史]] [[Category:松原市の歴史]] [[Category:仁徳天皇]]

It is a shrine for [[Gion worship]] dedicated to [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]].{{Cite web|last=Quin|first=Rebecca|date=2020-01-11|title=Namba Yasaka Shrine|url=https://travel.gaijinpot.com/namba-yasaka-shrine/|access-date=2023-05-13|website=GaijinPot Travel|language=en}} It has a large lion-shaped building which is famous in Japan.{{Cite web|title=Namba Yasaka Shrine|url=https://insideosaka.com/namba-yasaka-shrine/|access-date=2023-05-13|website=Inside Osaka|language=en-US}} Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == References == {{Reflist}} {{religion-stub}} [[:Category:Gion shrines]] [[:Category:Soja shrines]] [[:Category:Ken-sha]] [[:Category:Osaka]] [[:Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]]

Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. {{混同|難波八阪神社}} {{神社 |名称 = 難波神社 |画像 = [[画像:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|270px]]
拝殿 {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|type=point}} |所在地 = [[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[中央区 (大阪市)|中央区]][[博労町 (大阪市)|博労町]]4丁目1-3 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}} |祭神 = [[仁徳天皇]]、[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]] |社格 = 旧[[府社]] |創建 = 伝・[[反正天皇]]の時代 |例祭 = 秋祭（10月20日） |本殿 = |別名 = 難波上社 |神事 = }} '''難波神社'''（なんばじんじゃ）は、[[大阪市]][[中央区 (大阪市)|中央区]][[博労町 (大阪市)|博労町]]にある[[神社]]。旧[[近代社格制度|社格]]は[[府社]]。 == 概要 == [[摂津国]][[総社]]として難波大宮または平野神社、他にも上難波[[仁徳天皇]]宮、上難波神社、難波上宮ともいう。[[江戸時代]]には博労稲荷神社がある為に[[稲荷社]]と呼ばれていた。 [[アヤメ]]類（厳密な分類の[[ハナショウブ|花菖蒲]]）に縁のある神社で、6月にはあやめ祭（菖蒲神事）で花菖蒲を奉納する神事が執り行われている。境内で育った花菖蒲を御神前に御供えする神事。祭典中、菖蒲を刈り取る所作のある神楽「菖蒲刈り」が2人の巫女によって舞われる。 神紋は[[アヤメ#文様|菖蒲紋]]の一種『抱き菖蒲』（だきあやめ）。 == 歴史 == 創建は[[反正天皇]]の時代と伝えられ、当初は現在の[[大阪府]][[松原市]]に鎮座していたという。[[天慶]]6年（[[943年]]）に現・[[天王寺区]][[上本町]]に遷座する。 [[慶長]]2年（[[1597年]]）に[[豊臣秀吉]]の命令で、立退料2,000石をもらって現在地に遷座。しかし、慶長20年（[[1615年]]）の[[大坂の陣|大坂夏の陣]]後には[[江戸幕府]]によって境内地の9割を没収される。 [[明治]]時代になると[[府社]]に列せられている。[[1945年]]（[[昭和]]20年）3月13日・14日の第1回[[大阪大空襲]]で焼失するが、[[1974年]]（昭和49年）7月に再建される。 == 祭神 == * 主祭神：[[仁徳天皇]] * 配祀：[[スサノオ|素盞嗚尊]] == 境内 == * 本殿 - [[1974年]]（[[昭和]]49年）7月再建。 * 拝殿 - 1974年（昭和49年）7月再建。 * 博労[[稲荷神社]] - 祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂尊]]。摂社。商売繁盛の神様として[[船場]]の多くの商人から篤い信仰を受けていた。[[江戸時代]]を通じて難波神社は仁徳天皇を祀った神社としてではなく、博労稲荷神社がある神社として有名であり、難波神社のこと自体を指して「稲荷社」と呼んでいた。 * [[金刀比羅神社]] - 祭神：[[大物主]]神 * 十四柱相殿神社 - 祭神：左殿（[[豊臣秀吉]]公・[[菅原道真]]公・[[楠木正成]]公・[[徳川家康]]公）、中殿（[[トヨウケビメ|豊受姫大神]]・[[天照皇大神]]・[[応神天皇]]）、右殿（[[ミヅハノメ|水波能女大神]]・[[春日神|春日四柱大神]]・[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦大神]]・[[カグツチ|迦具土大神]]） * 社務所 == 祭礼 == * 2月節分 - 節分祭・玉の緒祭 * 6月8日 - 菖蒲神事 * 7月20・21日 - 夏祭・氷室祭 * 10月20日 - 例祭・秋祭 * 11月 - 火焚祭 * 毎月1日・2月節分 - 湯立神楽 == 文化財 == === 大阪市指定保存樹 === * 御神木の[[クスノキ|楠]] - 大阪市の保存樹第1号である。樹齢約400年。 == 関連項目 == * [[難波八阪神社]] - 別名：難波下社。 * [[生國魂神社]] - 別名：難波大社。 * [[高津宮]] - 難波神社と同様に[[仁徳天皇]]を主祭神とする。 == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Namba-jinja}} * [https://www.nanba-jinja.or.jp/ 難波神社]（公式HP） {{shinto-stub}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:なんはしんしや}} [[Category:大阪市の神社]] [[Category:総社 (地域)]] [[Category:稲荷神社]] [[Category:大阪府の旧府社]] [[Category:大阪市中央区の建築物]] [[Category:大阪市中央区の歴史]] [[Category:松原市の歴史]] [[Category:仁徳天皇]]

節分祭・玉の緒祭 * 6月8日 - 菖蒲神事 * 7月20・21日 - 夏祭・氷室祭 * 10月20日 - 例祭・秋祭 * 11月 - 火焚祭 * 毎月1日・2月節分 - 湯立神楽 == 文化財 == === 大阪市指定保存樹 === * 御神木の[[クスノキ|楠]] - 大阪市の保存樹第1号である。樹齢約400年。 == 関連項目 == * [[難波八阪神社]] - 別名：難波下社。 * [[生國魂神社]] - 別名：難波大社。 * [[高津宮]] - 難波神社と同様に[[仁徳天皇]]を主祭神とする。 == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Namba-jinja}} * [https://www.nanba-jinja.or.jp/ 難波神社]（公式HP） {{shinto-stub}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:なんはしんしや}} [[Category:大阪市の神社]] [[Category:総社 (地域)]] [[Category:稲荷神社]] [[Category:大阪府の旧府社]] [[Category:大阪市中央区の建築物]] [[Category:大阪市中央区の歴史]] [[Category:松原市の歴史]] [[Category:仁徳天皇]]

{{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine revision.text:
{{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine revision.text:
{{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine {{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{coordinates|34|40|44.3|N|135|29|58.4|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=難波神社}}|deity=[[Emperor Nintoku]]
all the [[kami]] of [[Settsu Province]] in its [[Soja shrine]]|type=[[Soja shrine]]}} Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a [[Shinto Shrine]] in [[Osaka]]. It worships [[Emperor Nintoku]].{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}} It was made by Nintoku's son [[Emperor Hanzei]]. In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}} The first theater for [[Bunraku]] puppet shows was built at the shrine.{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}} It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days. It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat. Some people think it was the [[Soja shrine]] of [[Settsu Province]]. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once. == History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, [[Emperor Hanzei|Hanzei]], in the ancient capital of [[Matsubara]] in [[Osaka Prefecture]]. On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor [[Emperor Go-Sanjō|Go-Sanjo]] visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses. Later, at the same time as [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] was building [[Osaka Castle]], Namba-jinja was moved to its current location. In the [[Edo period|Edo Period]] a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one. The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the [[World War II|Pacific War]] on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in [[reinforced concrete]] in 1974. ==Gallery== File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one. File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine
