Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka}}. It worships {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO">{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}}</ref> It was made by Nintoku's son {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Emperor Hanzei}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}}</ref>
The first theater for {{ill|Bunraku|en|Bunraku|WD=Q243170|lt=Bunraku}} puppet shows was built at the shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}}</ref>
It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
Some people think it was the [[Sōja shrine|Soja shrine]] of {{ill|Settsu Province|en|Settsu Province|WD=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province}}. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once.
== History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Hanzei}},<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> in the ancient capital of {{ill|Matsubara|en|Matsubara|WD=Q774952|lt=Matsubara}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}.<ref name=":0" />
On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor {{ill|Emperor Go-Sanjō|en|Emperor Go-Sanjō|WD=Q45844|lt=Go-Sanjo}} visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses.
Later, at the same time as {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was building {{ill|Osaka Castle|en|Osaka Castle|WD=Q321242|lt=Osaka Castle}}, Namba-jinja was moved to its current location.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period}} a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}} on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in {{ill|Reinforced concrete|en|Reinforced concrete|WD=Q184190|lt=Reinforced concrete}} in 1974.

It used to be more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine </gallery>

{{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{Coord|34.67897222|N|135.49955556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}|deity={{ill|Nintoku|WD=Q313119}}|type=[[Sōja shrine|Soja shrine]]|prefecture={{ill|Bakurō-machi|WD=Q60996404}}}}
Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka}}. It worships {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO">{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}}</ref> It was made by Nintoku's son {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Emperor Hanzei}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}}</ref>
The first theater for {{ill|Bunraku|en|Bunraku|WD=Q243170|lt=Bunraku}} puppet shows was built at the shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}}</ref>
It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
Some people think it was the [[Sōja shrine|Soja shrine]] of {{ill|Settsu Province|en|Settsu Province|WD=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province}}. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once.
== History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Hanzei}},<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> in the ancient capital of {{ill|Matsubara|en|Matsubara|WD=Q774952|lt=Matsubara}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}.<ref name=":0" />
On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor {{ill|Emperor Go-Sanjō|en|Emperor Go-Sanjō|WD=Q45844|lt=Go-Sanjo}} visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses.
Later, at the same time as {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was building {{ill|Osaka Castle|en|Osaka Castle|WD=Q321242|lt=Osaka Castle}}, Namba-jinja was moved to its current location.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period}} a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}} on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in {{ill|Reinforced concrete|en|Reinforced concrete|WD=Q184190|lt=Reinforced concrete}} in 1974.
==Gallery== <gallery mode="packed"> File:Namba Shinto Shrine in 201411.JPG|alt=|View of the shrine from the street File:Nanba Shrine1.jpg|alt=|Entrance Torii File:Namba Shinto Shrine at Night in 201412.JPG|alt=|Entrance Torii at night File:Futon daiko.jpg|alt=|Traditional Futon Daiko procession File:Nanba Shrine Bakurou Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Inari shrines|Inari shrine]] at Nanba Shrine. It used to be more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine </gallery>

}}

On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor {{ill|Emperor Go-Sanjō|en|Emperor Go-Sanjō|WD=Q45844|lt=Go-Sanjo}} visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses.

In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period}} a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />

{{Distinguish|Nanba Yasaka Shrine}}{{one source|date=May 2023}}{{Expand Japanese}}{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|coordinates={{Coord|34.67897222|N|135.49955556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}|deity={{ill|Nintoku|WD=Q313119|1=Emperor Nintoku}}|type=[[Sōja shrine|Soja shrine]]|prefecture={{ill|Bakurō-machi|WD=Q60996404|1=Bakurō-machi}}}}
Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} in {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka|1=Osaka}}. It worships {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO">{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}}</ref> It was made by Nintoku's son {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Emperor Hanzei|1=Emperor Hanzei}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}}</ref>
The first theater for {{ill|Bunraku|en|Bunraku|WD=Q243170|lt=Bunraku|1=Bunraku}} puppet shows was built at the shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}}</ref>
It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
Some people think it was the [[Sōja shrine|Soja shrine]] of {{ill|Settsu Province|en|Settsu Province|WD=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province|1=Settsu Province}}. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once.
== History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Hanzei|1=Emperor Hanzei}},<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> in the ancient capital of {{ill|Matsubara|en|Matsubara|WD=Q774952|lt=Matsubara|1=Matsubara}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}.<ref name=":0" />
On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor {{ill|Emperor Go-Sanjō|en|Emperor Go-Sanjō|WD=Q45844|lt=Go-Sanjo|1=Emperor Go-Sanjō}} visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses.
Later, at the same time as {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was building {{ill|Osaka Castle|en|Osaka Castle|WD=Q321242|lt=Osaka Castle|1=Osaka Castle}}, Namba-jinja was moved to its current location.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period|1=Edo period}} a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War|1=Pacific War}} on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in {{ill|Reinforced concrete|en|Reinforced concrete|WD=Q184190|lt=Reinforced concrete|1=Reinforced concrete}} in 1974.

It used to be more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> File:Nanba Shrine honsha.jpg|alt=|Main building of Nanba Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Juyonbashiraaidono Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small subshrine File:Nanba Shrine kotohira Shrine.jpg|alt=|A small [[Kotohira shrines|Kotohira Shrine]] at Nanba Shrine File:Nanba-jinjya Kusunoki.jpg|alt=|Kusunoki tree File:Naniwa-Schrein 1.jpg|alt=|Honden of the Shrine File:Nanba Shrine Roof from below.jpg|alt=|Roof of the Shrine File:Emblem on the door of Nanba shrine.jpg|alt=|Emblem on the door of the shrine File:Matsumoto Kiyoshi Senba Shinsaibashi.jpg|alt=|Shop across the street from Nanba Shrine </gallery>

Nanba Shrine (難波神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} in {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka|1=Osaka}}. It worships {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO">{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine|url=https://osaka-info.jp/en/spot/nanbajinja|access-date=2024-01-05|website=OSAKA INFO|language=en}}</ref> It was made by Nintoku's son {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Emperor Hanzei|1=Emperor Hanzei}}.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In Ancient Japan the capital city was wherever the emperor liked most. Nintoku had his capital in Osaka.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=KansaiOdyssey|date=2017-05-05|title=Famous Shrine near Namba: Kouzu Shrine|url=https://kansai-odyssey.com/kouzu-shrine/|access-date=2024-01-05|website=Kansai Odyssey|language=en-US}}</ref>
The first theater for {{ill|Bunraku|en|Bunraku|WD=Q243170|lt=Bunraku|1=Bunraku}} puppet shows was built at the shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}}</ref>
It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
Some people think it was the [[Sōja shrine|Soja shrine]] of {{ill|Settsu Province|en|Settsu Province|WD=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province|1=Settsu Province}}. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once.
== History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Hanzei|1=Emperor Hanzei}},<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> in the ancient capital of {{ill|Matsubara|en|Matsubara|WD=Q774952|lt=Matsubara|1=Matsubara}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}.<ref name=":0" />
On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor {{ill|Emperor Go-Sanjō|en|Emperor Go-Sanjō|WD=Q45844|lt=Go-Sanjo|1=Emperor Go-Sanjō}} visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses.
Later, at the same time as {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was building {{ill|Osaka Castle|en|Osaka Castle|WD=Q321242|lt=Osaka Castle|1=Osaka Castle}}, Namba-jinja was moved to its current location.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period|1=Edo period}} a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War|1=Pacific War}} on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in {{ill|Reinforced concrete|en|Reinforced concrete|WD=Q184190|lt=Reinforced concrete|1=Reinforced concrete}} in 1974.

The first theater for {{ill|Bunraku|en|Bunraku|WD=Q243170|lt=Bunraku|1=Bunraku}} puppet shows was built at the shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Namba Shrine in Osaka, Japan|url=https://www.gpsmycity.com/attractions/namba-shrine-30518.html|access-date=2024-01-05|website=GPSmyCity|language=en}}</ref>
It has a summer festival that starts on July 20th and lasts two days.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> It is called Himuro Matsuri and during the festival crushed ice is given to worshippers. It is believed that those who eat it will be protected from summer heat.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
Some people think it was the [[Sōja shrine|Soja shrine]] of {{ill|Settsu Province|en|Settsu Province|WD=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province|1=Settsu Province}}. Soja shrines are shrines where all the [[kami]] of a province can be worshipped at once.
== History == The shrine was built in 415, during the reign of the 18th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|en|Emperor Hanzei|WD=Q329769|lt=Hanzei|1=Emperor Hanzei}},<ref name="OSAKA INFO" /> in the ancient capital of {{ill|Matsubara|en|Matsubara|WD=Q774952|lt=Matsubara|1=Matsubara}} in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture|1=Osaka Prefecture}}.<ref name=":0" />
On New Year's Day 1071, Emperor {{ill|Emperor Go-Sanjō|en|Emperor Go-Sanjō|WD=Q45844|lt=Go-Sanjo|1=Emperor Go-Sanjō}} visited the shrine on his way to the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]], and he determined that, in addition to Nintoku, Susa-no-O (素盞嗚) and the female deity Uka-no-mi-tama (倉稲魂), for the treatment of illnesses.
Later, at the same time as {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|WD=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi|1=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} was building {{ill|Osaka Castle|en|Osaka Castle|WD=Q321242|lt=Osaka Castle|1=Osaka Castle}}, Namba-jinja was moved to its current location.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo Period|1=Edo period}} a small Inari shrine on the grounds called Bakurocho-no-Oinari-san was more famous than this one.<ref name="OSAKA INFO" />
The [[Torii]] and surrounding walls of the place of worship were destroyed during the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War|1=Pacific War}} on 14 March 1945 . They were rebuilt in {{ill|Reinforced concrete|en|Reinforced concrete|WD=Q184190|lt=Reinforced concrete|1=Reinforced concrete}} in 1974.
